To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the diffusion of water soluble macro-molecules through collagen is slowed by electro-static and hydrogen bonding between the individual macromolecular chain and collagen and that the extent of adsorption increases as the molecular weight increases.
diffusion of macromolecular drugs through collagen occurs rapidly and is slowed by electro-static and hydrophobic interactions with collagen.

the diffusion of angiotensins II, aldolase and albumin through collagen membranes is slowed by electro-static and hydrogen bonding between the diffusants and collagen, and the extent of binding is greater as the molecular weight is increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new drug delivery systems for the treatment of a variety of diseases, such as cancer, arthritis, and AIDS, using collagen as a matrix material.
understanding the mechanism of diffusion and sorption of proteins through connective tissue membranes and with the use of this information to develop collagen based controlled release systems.
the development and application of a novel drug delivery technology based on a collagen membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diffusion through collagen is slowed by the adsorption of macromolecular chains to collagen.
diffusion through collagen is slowed due to adsorption of macromolecules and that the diffusion coefficient of a given macromolecule is dependent on the molecular weight of that macromolecule.

the diffusion of water soluble macro molecules through collagen membranes occurs by a combination of two processes: (1) the diffusion of the macromolecule through the water filled channels in the collagen matrix; and (2) the diffusion of water through the collagen matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
collagen is a very good matrix for drug delivery.
diffusion of macromolecule through a collagen membrane is slowed as the molecular weight increases and as the swelling ratio of the collagen decreases.
diffusion through collagen is a combination of diffusion and sorption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diffusion of water soluble macro-molecules through collagen occurs through water filled spaces between collagen fibrils and that diffusion of macromole-cules is slowed by adsorption to collagen.

diffusion through collagen membranes is slowed down by electrostatic interactions between collagen and diffusant, and the extent of adsorption increases with the increase of molecular weight of the macromolecules.
the collagen is a porous material and diffusion through collagen is a function of the size of the molecule.
